label: K-Pass transport refund: standard rate
appliesTo: Registered K-Pass users, including foreign nationals who complete residence verification
why: A government transport subsidy that foreign residents are widely assumed to be excluded from, and are not — the barrier is registration and residence verification rather than nationality. The rates are also a live policy area rather than a fixed feature: the scheme was expanded in 2026 with additional tiers and a separate refund on spending above a threshold, so a figure quoted without a date is not much use.

history.source: Government of Korea — K-Pass scheme, operated within the 2026 unified travel card framework
history.note: Proportional refund of qualifying public transport spending. Higher tiers apply to young people, households with two children and older people at 30%, households with three or more children at 50%, and low-income users at 53.3%. A separate flat-amount refund applies to spending above a threshold. Registration is the gate for foreign nationals: the sign-up flow accepts a foreign registration number, with residence confirmed by document where automatic address verification is unavailable.
